title: Uncertainty calibration · the retained bootstrap failure
description: The nominal 95% percentile bootstrap covered 365 of 400 independent normal-mean calibration cases: 91.25%. Exact one-sided binomial coverage was enumerated separately.
uncertainty: Normal coverage has the archived Monte Carlo standard error; binomial coverage is exact enumeration up to floating-point rounding, not a finite Monte Carlo estimate. Values marginally above 1 from source rounding are preserved.
sampleUnit: 400 independent normal-mean coverage trials; fifteen exact binomial (n,p) calibration cells. These are numerical calibration cases, not physical spacetime samples.
assumptions: Calibration is independent of scientific state streams and did not tune the thresholds. Exact-binomial nominal per-cell coverage is 1−.05/3; normal-bootstrap nominal coverage is .95.
selection: One normal-coverage row and all fifteen binomial_exact_coverage rows. Missing n,p,standard errors or trial counts remain null; nominal coverage is the registered analytical level, not a fitted estimate.
